name: Saturday Night Two

date.source: Recapped by Primetime Central's own newsdesk on 27 January 2003 as the fed's own second Saturday Night; the day itself is not named.

evidence.note: The fed's own recap, carried whole under the line "Source: Twilight Slams": "The second Saturday Night kicked off at the Hartford Civic Center, and it was a night filled with surprises." Four segments are described — an opening interview, two matches, the on-air installation of a new Vice President, and a main event.

notes: The recap names the venue as the Hartford Civic Center and refers to the fed's own first Saturday Night as having run "last week." That first show is not named anywhere held and has no row.

name: Saturday Night — Uncasville

date.source: Previewed by Primetime Central's own newsdesk on 29 January 2003 as running "this Saturday Night"; the day is not named and no result was ever reported.

evidence.note: The fed's own preview, carried whole under the line "Source: Twilight Slams": a three-match card — Terrance Williams vs. the Outsider, Benjamin vs. Yeahboy, and Crazy Killer vs. Marcus Arelius in the main event with an unannounced guest commentator — "live from Mohegan Sun Hotel and Casino in Uncasville, Connecticut this Saturday Night live on public access television from Twilight Slams!"

notes: Previewed match by match; nothing held reports whether it ran. The fed's own weekly carried no distinguishing name of its own, so this row is named for the venue its preview billed.

name: Hell in Your House

date.source: Named once, in the past tense, by Primetime Central's own newsdesk of 29 January 2003; nothing held dates it.

evidence.note: Named in the fed's own preview of its Uncasville card, on a debut that had not happened: "Could it be Samba Tatenaka? The Japanese hybrid was supposed to enter at the 'Hell in Your House' pay-per-view."

notes: A pay-per-view the fed's own copy names once and never returns to. Nothing held says whether it ran.
